ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The top diagram shows an unfolded square sheet with exactly two small holes. Both holes are in the lower-left part of the square; one hole is slightly higher and farther left, and the other is lower and farther right, so the segment joining them slopes downward to the right. The answer choices show possible dotted fold lines: A has crossing diagonals, B and E have vertical dotted lines, C has a vertical and horizontal center line, and D has diagonal dotted lines sloping upward to the right. Reasoning: A single hole punched through folded paper produces two holes after unfolding that are mirror images across the fold crease. Therefore, the fold line must be the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting the two holes. Since the segment between the two observed holes slopes downward to the right, the fold line must slope upward to the right and pass midway between the holes. Among the options, only D has a diagonal fold line with that orientation and plausible placement. So the correct choice is D.
